title: 贫女
author: 秦韬玉
intro: A poor girl with real skill and good taste cannot find a husband, because everyone admires flashy fashion — so year after year she embroiders other women’s wedding dresses. The last line gave Chinese the phrase “making wedding clothes for others”.
analysis: 诗用一个贫家女子的口吻说话。她住在草房子里，从没穿过绫罗绸缎；想托媒人说亲，又更加自伤身世。谁会欣赏她高雅的品格呢？大家喜欢的都是时下流行的打扮。她敢夸自己一双手针线活最好，却不愿意把眉毛画得长长的去和别人比美。最让她痛苦的是：年年拿着金线刺绣，却都是在给别人缝做嫁衣。表面上写贫女嫁不出去，其实是写有才华的读书人：品德好、本领大，却因为出身低、不会讨好，一直得不到重用，只能替别人做事、为别人出力。这种借女子写读书人的手法，在古诗里很常见。“为他人作嫁衣裳”后来变成常用语，比喻白白为别人辛苦忙碌。
analysisEn: The poem speaks in the voice of a poor young woman. She lives behind a door of woven brush and has never worn fine silk. She would like to ask a matchmaker to find her a husband, but even thinking about it makes her feel worse about her lot. Who appreciates real grace and taste? Everyone admires whatever style of make-up is in fashion. She is proud of her ten skilful fingers and her fine needlework, but she refuses to compete with other girls by painting her eyebrows longer. What hurts most is this: year after year she embroiders with gold thread, and every piece is someone else’s wedding dress. On the surface the poem is about a girl who cannot marry. Readers have always understood it as being about talented scholars from humble families — honest and capable, but unwilling to flatter, and so never given a chance, while they spend their lives working for others’ success. Using a woman’s situation to speak about a scholar’s career is a long tradition in Chinese poetry. The last line became a common saying: 为他人作嫁衣裳, “to make wedding clothes for others”, means working hard only for someone else’s benefit.
background: Qin Taoyu was a late-Tang poet whose dates are unknown. He failed the examinations for years and is said to have been granted the jinshi degree only in 882, by special decree, after following the emperor Xizong to Sichuan during Huang Chao’s rebellion. This is by far his best-known poem.
pronunciation: 绮罗 qǐ luó；格调 gé diào；“为他人作嫁衣裳”的“为”读 wèi（替）；“压金线”的“压”读 yā（刺绣的一种针法）。末句“衣裳”的“裳”是韵脚，读 cháng，与香、伤、妆、长押韵（口语读 yīshang）。
version: 采用通行版本（如《唐诗三百首》所收）。“敢将十指夸针巧”的“针巧”，有的版本作“偏巧”；“共怜时世俭梳妆”的“俭”，一说通“险”，指奇异的时髦打扮；网站用“针巧”“俭”，按“时髦的打扮”理解。

lines.py: péng mén wèi shí qǐ luó xiāng
lines.lit: Behind a brushwood door, I have never known the fragrance of fine silk;
lines.en: Behind my door of woven brush I’ve never worn scented silk;

lines.py: nǐ tuō liáng méi yì zì shāng
lines.lit: thinking of asking a good matchmaker only hurts me more.
lines.en: just thinking of a matchmaker makes me sadder still.

lines.py: shuí ài fēng liú gāo gé diào
lines.lit: Who loves elegance and a lofty style?
lines.en: Who cares for true grace and taste?

lines.py: gòng lián shí shì jiǎn shū zhuāng
lines.lit: All admire the make-up fashionable in these times.
lines.en: Everyone admires whatever look is in fashion.

lines.py: gǎn jiāng shí zhǐ kuā zhēn qiǎo
lines.lit: I dare boast that my ten fingers are skilled with the needle,
lines.en: I’ll boast my ten fingers sew better than anyone’s,

lines.py: bù bǎ shuāng méi dòu huà cháng
lines.lit: but I will not compete in painting my two eyebrows long.
lines.en: but I won’t paint my brows longer just to outshine the others.

lines.py: kǔ hèn nián nián yā jīn xiàn
lines.lit: Bitterly I resent, year after year, stitching with gold thread
lines.en: What hurts is this: year after year I stitch with gold thread,

lines.py: wèi tā rén zuò jià yī cháng
lines.lit: to make wedding clothes for other people.
lines.en: making wedding gowns for other brides.

words.en: a door made of brushwood — a poor home
words.note: 比喻穷人家；今天有成语“蓬荜生辉”（客气话，说客人来让寒舍增光）。
指华贵的丝织品，代指富贵生活。
“媒”今天说“媒人”“做媒”，也有“媒体”。
古义“更加”，今天有“日益”“精益求精”。
古义是高雅脱俗；今天多指男女关系，意思变了。
今天仍常用，如“格调高雅”。
古义：“怜”是爱，不是今天“可怜”的意思。

words.en: to stitch with gold thread (an embroidery technique)
words.note: 刺绣的一种手法，把金线压在布面上缝住。

words.en: to make wedding clothes for others — to work only for others’ benefit
words.note: 今天仍常说，常简化为“为人作嫁”。

imagery.name: 线
imagery.zh: 金线代表贫女精湛的手艺，可一针一线都绣在别人的嫁衣上，成了“才华为别人所用”的象征。
imagery.en: The gold thread shows her fine craft — yet every stitch goes into another bride’s dress, a picture of talent spent only for others.
